rv.q: Mr. Matthau and Mr. Lemmon may be gone, but their spirits hover benevolently over this production, which finds Nathan Lane and Matthew Broderick stepping into those immortal mismatched shoes with obvious relish and mostly satisfying results.
Mr. Lane and Mr. Broderick are both gifted comic actors, but they're playing against type here, and the results are mixed at best.

Everything that was originally oh-so-right about the set-up — a divorced man and a divorcing man share digs and ultimately begin replicating the dynamic of their marriages — is still hilariously right.
